governance.note: All active levers trace to measured inputs. The new lever is a per-year measured marginal-heat-rate anchor on MISO's PJM NeighborInterface (hr_by_year={2023:11.2, 2024:13.49, 2025:12.18}), derived by scripts/derive_neighbor_hr_by_year.py --iso MISO from PJM's OWN realized RT LMP (actual_lmp_hourly_PJM.parquet) divided by Henry Hub x the load-shape convexity K — i.e. PJM's realized implied market heat rate each year. This is a measured neighbor price-formation input (rule #12): the forward analogue is the structural marginal_heat_rate used whenever a year has no measured LMP, and the derivation never sees MISO's own interchange flow (rule #11). It replaces the flat 3-year mean (12.3) that under-priced the PJM hub in dear-gas 2024 (measured 13.49) and drove the largest MISO seam to over-import. Other measured levers unchanged from the MISO config: priced import/export node served by the reference-price interface (neighbor gas x heat-rate x load-shape, hurdle in $/MWh), Manitoba firm-hydro import block (firm contract, floored must-flow in MISO-North), per-plant CAMPD tranche binning, historic CAMPD unit-outage windows (exogenous availability), measured F923 per-plant monthly delivered fuel, EIA-923 biomass must-run profile. No adder/haircut/sigmoid tuned to the price or volume residual; no unit pinned to its observed CEMS generation; no input rescaled so the model output lands on actuals.
governance.open_misses_note: Honest open structural misses (not addressed by this lever, documented not masked): (1) systematic net over-import persists in all years (2023 model 63.6 vs actual 37.9 TWh net import; 2024 48.3 vs 23.1 after the anchor improved it from 60.3) — the SPP (flat HR 10.0) and South/SOCO (flat 12.0) seams remain un-anchored and the import-node level over-serves; (2) 2025 net-interchange still sign-flips (model +7.5 net export vs actual -19 net import) driven by the 2025 coal over-run (235 vs 192 TWh) making MISO long, a coal-offer / merit-order root cause the PJM anchor (12.18 ~ flat) does not touch; (3) CORRECTION (supersedes the earlier note on this run): CT_PEAKER is a REAL under-generation, NOT resolved. EIA-923 actual MISO CT_PEAKER (simple-cycle GT/IC) is 16.9 / 18.95 / ~19 TWh for 2023/2024/2025; the model's 2.97 TWh (3.9% CF) in 2024 is a ~16 TWh under-dispatch, not the actual reserve level. The classifier is CORRECT and CONSISTENT on both sides: the model fleet's plant_group (fleet.py _map_fuel_type + plant_taxonomy.classify_plant) and the EIA-923 benchmark (_classify_f923 -> classify_plant) both route combined-cycle CT-prime-mover codes (CT/CA/CS/CC) into CC_REGULAR and only GT/IC into CT_PEAKER, so there is NO CC->CT contamination and no classification bug. The MISO-only ct_mustrun_floor_mwh_by_plant sum = 18.95 TWh, exactly equal to the EIA-923 CT_PEAKER benchmark; the '114 TWh' cited earlier was the NATIONWIDE floor sum (the function is national, keyed by plant_id, and only MISO fleet plants are actually floored). --ct-mustrun-per-plant was correctly REJECTED, but for the right reason: the floor pins CT to its observed EIA-923 monthly output, a rule #12 actuals-pin with no forward analogue, NOT a classification artifact. The real fix for the CT under-generation is merit-order: cheap over-imports plus (formerly) nuclear-at-full-nameplate fill the bottom of the stack and price peakers out; fixing the injection errors lets CT clear. The nuclear over-injection is addressed by the nuclear-derate run (miso10); the over-import remains the dominant open injection error. (4) scarcity tail absent (0 h >$200 vs 30/37/88). The remaining items are the next levers, not residual fits.
